identity.title: Solar ALMA Observations: Constraining the Chromosphere above Sunspots

paper_type_evidence.quote: obtained during the solar ALMA Science Verification campaign in 2015, and compare them with the predictions of semi-empirical sunspot umbral/penumbral atmosphere models.

evidence.quote: AR12470, which was located in the eastern hemisphere (N13E30) on December 16, and north of disc center (N15E05) on December 18.

question.value: What do ALMA 1.3 mm and 3 mm brightness temperatures of a sunspot umbra and penumbra imply for semi-empirical sunspot chromosphere models?

evidence.quote: we extend their analysis by comparing ALMA observations of the same sunspot at two different millimeter wavelengths with the predictions of sunspot umbral and, for the first time, penumbral models.
ADS/JAO.ALMA$\sharp$2011.0.00020.SV

bands.value: Band 3 (3 mm) on 2015 Dec 16; Band 6 (1.3 mm) on 2015 Dec 18

evidence.quote: Band 3 (100 GHz, corresponding to a wavelength of 3 mm), and on 2015 December 18 in Band 6 (230 GHz, 1.3 mm)

arrays.value: twenty-two 12m antennae and nine 7m ACA antennae, plus single-dish full-disk scanning

evidence.quote: a compact array configuration which included twenty-two 12m antennae and nine 7m antennae of the Atacama Compact Array (ACA).
was 4.9$''$ $\times$2.2$''$ and 2.4$''$ $\times$0.9$''$ at 3 mm and 1.3 mm, respectively.
The ALMA observations were carried out on 2015 December 16 in Band 3
Using ALMA Science Verification data (cite: 2017ApJ...841L..20I), hereafter Paper I

provided.value: Continuum, magnetograms and UV/EUV images used to define umbra/penumbra boundaries and for comparison

evidence.quote: The umbral and penumbral boundaries were derived from the HMI continuum image as, respectively, 0.65 and 0.90 of the surrounding photospheric white-light intensity

what.value: Earlier sunspot brightness measurements (BIMA 3.5 mm, JCMT, Nobeyama, NoRH) for comparison

evidence.quote: the measurements from JCMT at 0.35, 0.85 and 1.2 mm (diamonds) made by (cite: 1995ApJ...453..517L) at a resolution of 14-17$''$

what.value: 3 mm umbral/penumbral brightness from Paper I

evidence.quote: and in Fig. 5 from Paper I.

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Published semi-empirical umbral and penumbral atmosphere models (Avrett 1981, Maltby 1986, Severino 1994, Socas-Navarro 2007, Fontenla 2009, Avrett 2015, de la Cruz Rodriguez 2016; YBB, DF, FCHHT-R, S-N D; FALC for QS)

evidence.quote: In this work we build on the same set of umbral models as in (cite: 2014A&A...561A.133L).

archive_products_used_as_is.value: Interferometric and single-dish data combined via feathering, as in Paper I

evidence.quote: The single dish and interferometric data were further combined in the UV plane via feathering to derive the absolute brightness temperature of the interferometric maps

flux_scale_uncertainty.value: ~100 K absolute; relative 4 K (3 mm), 10 K (1.3 mm)

evidence.quote: we adopt an uncertainty of order 100 K in the absolute temperatures.

array_combination.value: Feathering of single-dish and interferometric maps

evidence.quote: combined in the UV plane via feathering
The full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) of the synthesized beam was 4.9$''$ $\times$2.2$''$
Details of the observations and image synthesis can be found in Paper I.

what.value: Umbra/penumbra boundaries at 0.65 and 0.90 of photospheric intensity

evidence.quote: 0.65 and 0.90 of the surrounding photospheric white-light intensity following (cite: 2007A&A...465..291M)
The details of the mm brightness calculations can be found in, e.g., (cite: 2004A&A...419..747L).

unstated_but_needed: Calibration pipeline/CASA version and feathering parameters
Exact ellipse parameters for inner/outer umbra and penumbra
Code for the free-free brightness computation
Details of how model QS references were subtracted per model

method.value: Umbral and penumbral boundaries from HMI continuum; inner/outer regions chosen by eye with ellipses

evidence.quote: red and green ellipses outlining inner and outer umbral boundaries (chosen by eye as described below)
0.65 and 0.90 of the surrounding photospheric white-light intensity
The inner umbral ellipse, depicted in red, corresponds to the region of the strongest LOS magnetic field

method.value: Mean and RMS of pixel brightness temperatures per region, with maps normalized to single-dish QS values

evidence.quote: we determined typical brightness temperature values as the average of the corresponding set and its root-mean-square (RMS) variation

assumptions.value: Disk-center QS ~6000 K (1.3 mm) and ~7400 K (3 mm)

evidence.quote: around 6000 K and 7400 K, at 1.3 mm and 3 mm, respectively

method.value: Thermal free-free emission with H-zero and H-minus opacities at 32 wavelengths, 0.1-20 mm; effective formation heights from contribution function centroids

evidence.quote: We have calculated the expected submm/mm brightness temperatures at 32 selected wavelengths in the range 0.1–20 mm for sunspot umbral models
assuming that the thermal free-free mechanism is responsible for the emission at mm wavelengths

method.value: Compare model-minus-QS difference spectra with observed brightness minus disk-center QS, including earlier observations

evidence.quote: we plot the difference spectra between the umbral brightness and the QS brightness from the corresponding reference atmospheric models

evidence.loc: Millimeter-wavelength brightness spectra from umbral models
evidence.quote: None of the depicted model curves provides an outstanding fit to the observations at these longer wavelengths. However, the umbral model of (cite: 1994ASIC..433..169S), depicted in Fig. 12 by a red curve, shows the best agreement

results_numeric.quantity: Effective formation height, Severino 1994 model, 1.3 mm / 3 mm

evidence.quote: | Severino et al. 1994             |     1090      |     1540      |

findings_qualitative.value: Umbra looks very different at 1.3 and 3 mm, while penumbral structure is similar at both

evidence.quote: We find that the sunspot umbra exhibits a radically different appearance at 1.3 mm and 3 mm, whereas the penumbral brightness structure is similar at the two wavelengths.

claims.hypothesis: Do existing umbral models reproduce ALMA mm brightness of sunspot umbra?
claims.experiment: Compared ALMA inner-umbra brightness differences to model-predicted spectra
claims.result: Severino et al. (1994) model fits best
claims.finding: Best umbral model is Severino et al. (1994)

evidence.quote: Among the tested umbral models, that of (cite: 1994ASIC..433..169S) provides the best fit to the observational data

claims.hypothesis: Do penumbral models reproduce ALMA data?
claims.experiment: Compared penumbral brightness to four models
claims.result: YBB and FCHHT R closest but not satisfactory

evidence.quote: No penumbral model amongst those considered here gives a satisfactory fit to the currently available measurements.

limitations_admitted.value: Side lobes may affect 1.3 mm umbral brightness, which should be treated as an upper limit

evidence.quote: the derived umbral brightness depression in the single-dish map at 1.3 mm should be considered as an upper limit

referee_caveats_inferred: Single sunspot on two different days
Beam resolution comparable to umbral size, so region averages are partly smeared

evidence.quote: This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA$\sharp$2011.0.00020.SV.
